analysis.title: GS MORNING: 2 Mins Read on Equities, Rich Privo's Risk Views, Latest FX Trader, Implications of FCI Tightening, and Week Ahead Previews
key_insights: GS strategists frame the key equity question as where earnings come from next once AI infrastructure and capex build-out hands off the baton. Q3 S&P 500 earnings growth was over 35%, so the worry is forward looking.

Tech-heavy indices (NDX, SOX, Info Tech) are oversold with valuations at >10 year lows (NDX 17x fwd P/E, SOX/Semis about 12-13x). Conditions for a bounce exist but year-end rally optimism has faded on a lack of catalysts.

Charts suggest cuts in AI supply chain names while companies point to rising estimate revisions ahead of DELL, MU, AVGO and HPE earnings. This charts-versus-companies conflict makes stepping in harder.

Dom Wilson cites cracks in the AI story: financing needs, a possible peak in the investment impulse, slowing capex upgrades, credit pressure, a fresh Fed tightening cycle and a political shift. No single macro worry yet, so the floor is unclear.

Prime brokerage data show fundamental L/S net leverage at 42.3% (1st percentile 1-year) and beta-adjusted net at 48.2% (5-year low). Shorting was the largest since April 2025, so a bear market rally setup is obvious.

VIX nearly touched 40, CNN Fear & Greed is about 10, put/call is near the 95th percentile and the VIX curve is at its steepest inversion since April 2025. Historically VIX closes above 35 often preceded positive equity reversals over following weeks.
Privorotsky says credit is the tell. If Nvidia rallies while neocloud spreads stay under pressure, it is probably short covering rather than a real recovery in risk appetite.

Asia support measures over the weekend: China lowering margin requirements, Korea easing buyback restrictions, Taiwan tightening short selling rules. Described as sticking plasters not typical of a bottom.

GS FX: a hawkish US policy shock lifted the Dollar against G10, then growth worries rotated Dollar strength into EM, the most painful type for cyclical FX. GS sees the Dollar softening only gradually in 2027.
GS FX likes COP and ZAR on domestic fundamentals and is focused on relative policy in AUD and CAD.
GS FCI has tightened about 100bp this year, all since early September and over 40bp last week. Persistent tightening is estimated to drag 2027 Q4/Q4 GDP growth by 0.5pp.

GS Economics sees a second Fed hike in December as a near certainty and still expects a third hike in March. Further tightening led by risk sentiment or AI spending concerns could displace hikes next year.
Week ahead: PMIs Monday, AUD CPI and US PCE Wednesday, BOK Thursday. GS expects a hawkish hold from the BOK versus a consensus 25bp hike.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech indices are oversold with valuations at >10 year lows, extreme positioning and vol, and Q3 earnings growth over 35%. Estimate revisions are expected to rise.
tension_points.bear_case: Charts signal cuts, capex upgrades are slowing, credit is under pressure, and the Fed is hiking. A rally may be only short covering.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nvidia rallying while neocloud spreads remain under pressure would signal only short covering, not recovery.

theme_stances.key_argument: Extreme positioning, elevated vol and oversold valuations create a compelling tactical setup for a bounce.
FCI tightening equals about 100bp of hikes, but high inflation and above-potential growth keep a March hike expected.
